title: Google Research ASPEST: Bridging Active Sample Acquisition & Selective Prediction via Checkpoint Ensembles
author: ontology-spider-learning-wave

edges.description: Subproject active_selective_prediction (ASPEST, arXiv:2304.03870) surfaced by Ontology-Spider .dialog query
Informs selective abstention and ensemble disagreement thresholding in uncertainty_guard
Extends UQ shift benchmarks with active oracle labeling and checkpoint-ensemble self-training

claims.assertion: active_selective_prediction evaluates active adaptation and selective abstention across six domain-shift benchmarks (mnist->svhn, cifar10->cinic10, fmow, amazon_review, domainnet, otto).

ASPEST maintains a checkpoint ensemble (update_ensemble_state), queries bounded label budgets via AverageMarginSampling over test shifts, self-trains with KL-divergence only on samples within a gated confidence band [lower_threshold, upper_threshold), and scores abstention from max ensemble probability.

distilled_learning: Combine low-budget human oracle labeling (average-margin sampling) with dual-thresholded KL self-training over running checkpoint ensembles so selective prediction abstention thresholds stay calibrated under target distribution shift.
